paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation: This line plot, titled "Answer Change Percentage by Initial Accuracy," illustrates the average percentage change in answers over seven turns for two initial answer types: "Initial Correct Answer" and "Initial Incorrect Answer." The x-axis, labeled "Turn Number," uses a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7, with tick labels appearing at each integer. The y-axis, labeled "Average Change Percentage (%)," uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 50, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 10 percentage points. The plot displays two lines: the "Initial Correct Answer" is represented by a solid red line with circular markers, starting at approximately 3% change in turn 1, rising to 11% in turn 4, and remaining constant at 11% through turn 7. The "Initial Incorrect Answer" is represented by a solid orange line with circular markers, starting at approximately 17% change in turn 1, rising sharply to 50% in turn 4, and remaining constant at 50% through turn 7.
